slides.say: A video game starts with a hundred sixty players. At the end of each level, three quarters of the players who began that level are still in the game. How many players are still in the game after two levels?
Here we just have to understand what they want, and calculate. We'll solve it two ways, the math way level by level, and then with an insight, writing the whole exercise first.

Let's start with the math way. A hundred sixty players start level one. At the end of the level, three quarters of them are still in. Let's picture them as a bar, cut into four equal parts. Three of the parts stay.
at: Let's picture them as a bar

slides.say: One part is a quarter of a hundred sixty. Half of a hundred sixty is eighty, and half again is forty. So one part is forty, and three parts are three times forty, a hundred twenty.

Careful, this is where the trap is. If we took forty away twice, we'd get eighty, choice number two. But level two works on the players who began level two, a hundred twenty, not a hundred sixty. So now a hundred twenty players are the whole bar.
at: If we took forty away twice

slides.say: A quarter of a hundred twenty is thirty, and three quarters is three times thirty, ninety. So ninety players are still in the game after two levels. Choice number three is our answer.
at: A quarter of a hundred twenty
Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now the insight. We start again from the givens. Instead of calculating as we go, let's first write the whole exercise. A hundred sixty, times three quarters for level one, times three quarters for level two.
at: A hundred sixty, times three quarters

slides.say: We multiply the fractions. Three times three is nine on top. Four times four is sixteen on the bottom. So it's a hundred sixty times nine sixteenths.
at: So it's a hundred sixty times

slides.say: And now it's easy to see. A hundred sixty divided by sixteen is ten. And ten times nine is ninety.
at: A hundred sixty divided by sixteen

slides.say: So when a question has several stages, don't rush to calculate each one. Write the whole exercise first. Then check whether you can simplify before multiplying. Choice number three is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
